statement: A random vector x = (x_1, ..., x_k) is k-variate (jointly, multivariate) normally distributed if every linear combination of its k components has a univariate normal distribution.

symbols.dimensions: q x q, q x (k-q), (k-q) x q, (k-q) x (k-q)

symbols.meaning: constant offset vector and constant matrix of an affine map Y = c + Bx

properties.property: The distribution of x_1 conditional on x_2 = a is itself multivariate normal, (x_1 | x_2 = a) ~ N(μ̄, Σ̄), with μ̄ = μ_1 + Σ_12 Σ_22^{-1}(a - μ_2) and Σ̄ = Σ_11 - Σ_12 Σ_22^{-1} Σ_21 (the Schur complement of Σ_22 in Σ).
properties.why: obtained by partitioning μ and Σ and inverting the overall covariance, dropping the conditioned rows/columns, and inverting back

properties.property: Marginal distributions are obtained by simply dropping the marginalized-out variables from μ and Σ; the marginal is again multivariate normal (e.g. for x' = [x_1, x_3], μ' = [μ_1, μ_3] and Σ' has blocks Σ_11, Σ_13, Σ_31, Σ_33).
properties.why: follows from the definition of the multivariate normal and linear algebra

properties.property: Any affine transformation Y = c + Bx of x ~ N(μ, Σ) is again multivariate normal: Y ~ N(c + Bμ, BΣB^T).
properties.why: affine images of a jointly Gaussian vector are jointly Gaussian

properties.property: If X and Y are each normally distributed and independent, then (X, Y) is jointly normal; conversely a jointly normal pair need not be independent, only so if uncorrelated (ρ = 0).
properties.why: independence is sufficient but not necessary for joint normality

properties.property: Within a multivariate normal vector, any two or more components that are uncorrelated are independent (hence pairwise independence implies independence for jointly Gaussian components).
properties.why: uncorrelatedness plus joint Gaussianity is a special case where independence follows, unlike the general case

assumptions.assumption: Σ is a valid (positive semi-definite) covariance matrix for the vector; Σ_22^{-1} in the conditioning formula is taken as the generalized inverse when Σ_22 is singular.
assumptions.breaks_when: Σ_22 is singular and only the generalized inverse is used, the conditional covariance formula still holds but ordinary matrix inversion is unavailable

failure_modes.mode: Assuming marginal normality of each component implies joint normality of the vector
failure_modes.signature: X and Y are each individually normal, but (X, Y) is not bivariate normal
failure_modes.cause: joint normality is a strictly stronger condition than each component being marginally normal; a counterexample is X ~ N(0,1) with Y = X for |X| > c and Y = -X for |X| < c

failure_modes.mode: Assuming uncorrelated implies independent in general
failure_modes.signature: two random variables have zero correlation but are still statistically dependent
failure_modes.cause: uncorrelatedness implies independence only when the variables are jointly (multivariate) normal; in general uncorrelated variables can be dependent
